page: Microsoft Azure M64 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz and includes 38 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core, alongside 7340 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by a tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10% across stress-ng, gzip compression, and Geekbench tests. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall within the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance in the top 25% for large-block uncached read operations, while small-block cached reads and large-block writes remain average.

Given its massive 1 TB memory capacity and 7.3 TB local storage, the M64 is designed for memory-intensive workloads rather than compute-bound single-threaded tasks. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching layers, and enterprise resource planning systems that require high memory density and substantial local storage. However, for workloads dependent on high single-core throughput or GPU acceleration, other instance families may offer better resource-to-performance alignment.
description: Microsoft Azure M64 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 2.7 GHz, paired with 1024.0 GB of RAM and 7340 GB of local storage. Benchmark data highlights a significant tradeoff: single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core performance and database operations sit in the average middle 50% range. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is strong, placing in the top 25%. With 16.0 GB of memory per core and substantial local storage, this instance is structured for memory-heavy and storage-reliant workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory data stores, and enterprise applications that prioritize high memory capacity and local storage over raw single-threaded compute speed.
